title: TARP capital injection on bank risk-taking

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with Event Study**

The classic DID framework is appropriate here: we have a clear treatment (TARP capital injection in 2008-2009), a binary treatment group (recipient vs. non-recipient banks), and panel data spanning pre- and post-treatment periods.

**Key identifying assumption:** Parallel pre-trends — absent TARP, recipient and non-recipient banks would have followed the same trajectory in non-performing loan ratios. This is testable in the pre-period using an event-study specification.

**Threats to identification:**
- **Selection bias:** TARP recipients were not randomly assigned — banks in worse condition or deemed systemically important were more likely to receive funds. DID addresses time-invariant differences via bank fixed effects, and common shocks via time fixed effects.
- **Moral hazard channel:** If TARP capital cushions reduced the cost of risk-taking, we'd expect a positive DID coefficient (higher NPL ratio for treated banks post-injection).

I will estimate:
1. A standard two-way fixed effects DID model
2. An event-study specification to verify parallel pre-trends
3. Robustness checks including clustered standard errors and alternative specifications

## 2. R Code

```r
# =============================================================
# TARP Capital Injection and Bank Risk-Taking: DID Analysis
# =============================================================

library(fixest)    # For TWFE, event study, clustered SEs
library(data.table)

# --- Load data ---
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s04_data.csv")

cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows x", ncol(df), "cols\n")
cat("Banks:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated banks:", length(unique(df$unit_id[df$treated == 1])), "\n")
cat("Control banks:", length(unique(df$unit_id[df$treated == 0])), "\n\n")

# Identify the treatment timing
# post=1 starts at some period; find it
post_periods <- df[post == 1, sort(unique(period))]
pre_periods  <- df[post == 0, sort(unique(period))]
cat("Pre-periods:", pre_periods, "\n")
cat("Post-periods:", post_periods, "\n\n")

# --- Summary statistics ---
cat("=== Summary Statistics: Mean NPL Ratio ===\n")
summ <- df[, .(mean_y = mean(y), sd_y = sd(y), n = .N), 
           by = .(treated, post)]
print(summ)

# Raw DID calculation
y_treat_pre  <- summ[treated == 1 & post == 0, mean_y]
y_treat_post <- summ[treated == 1 & post == 1, mean_y]
y_ctrl_pre   <- summ[treated == 0 & post == 0, mean_y]
y_ctrl_post  <- summ[treated == 0 & post == 1, mean_y]
raw_did <- (y_treat_post - y_treat_pre) - (y_ctrl_post - y_ctrl_pre)
cat("\nRaw DID estimate:", round(raw_did, 4), "\n\n")

# =============================================================
# MODEL 1: Standard DID with Two-Way Fixed Effects
# =============================================================
cat("=== MODEL 1: TWFE DID ===\n")
mod1 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
              data = df, 
              cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(mod1)

cat("\n*** DID Coefficient (treat_x_post):", 
    round(coef(mod1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "***\n")
cat("*** Standard Error (clustered by bank):", 
    round(se(mod1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "***\n")
cat("*** t-statistic:", 
    round(tstat(mod1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "***\n")
cat("*** p-value:", 
    round(pvalue(mod1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "***\n\n")

# =============================================================
# MODEL 2: Event Study — Test Parallel Pre-Trends
# =============================================================
cat("=== MODEL 2: Event Study ===\n")

# Create relative time variable
# Assume treatment starts at the first post period
treat_start <- min(post_periods)
df[, rel_time := period - treat_start]

cat("Treatment starts at period:", treat_start, "\n")
cat("Relative time values:", sort(unique(df$rel_time)), "\n")

# Interact treated with each relative time period
# Omit rel_time = -1 as reference period
df[, rel_time_factor := factor(rel_time)]

mod2 <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
              data = df,
              cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(mod2)

# Extract event-study coefficients
es_coefs <- coef(mod2)
es_se    <- se(mod2)
cat("\n=== Event Study Coefficients ===\n")
for (i in seq_along(es_coefs)) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s: %.4f (SE=%.4f, p=%.4f)\n", 
              names(es_coefs)[i], es_coefs[i], es_se[i], pvalue(mod2)[i]))
}

# Test for parallel pre-trends: joint F-test on pre-treatment interactions
pre_trend_names <- grep("rel_time::-[2-9]|rel_time::-[1-9][0-9]", 
                        names(coef(mod2)), value = TRUE)
cat("\nPre-treatment coefficients to test:", pre_trend_names, "\n")

if (length(pre_trend_names) > 0) {
  pre_test <- wald(mod2, keep = pre_trend_names)
  cat("\n=== Joint F-test for Parallel Pre-Trends ===\n")
  print(pre_test)
}

# Plot event study
cat("\n=== Event Study Plot ===\n")
tryCatch({
  iplot(mod2, main = "Event Study: TARP Effect on NPL Ratio",
        xlab = "Quarters Relative to TARP",
        ylab = "Effect on NPL Ratio")
}, error = function(e) cat("Plot display skipped in non-interactive mode.\n"))

# =============================================================
# MODEL 3: Robustness — OLS DID without fixed effects
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== MODEL 3: Robustness — Pooled OLS DID ===\n")
mod3 <- feols(y ~ treated * post, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(mod3)

# =============================================================
# MODEL 4: Robustness — Add bank-specific linear time trends
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== MODEL 4: Robustness — Bank-Specific Time Trends ===\n")
mod4 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id[period] + period, 
              data = df, 
              cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(mod4)
cat("DID with bank-specific trends:", round(coef(mod4)["treat_x_post"], 4), 
    "(SE:", round(se(mod4)["treat_x_post"], 4), ")\n")

# =============================================================
# MODEL 5: Robustness — Double-clustered SEs (bank & period)
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== MODEL 5: Robustness — Double-Clustered SEs ===\n")
mod5 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
              data = df, 
              cluster = ~unit_id + period)
summary(mod5)

# =============================================================
# Summary comparison
# =============================================================
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("=== SUMMARY OF ALL SPECIFICATIONS ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
etable(mod1, mod3, mod4, mod5, 
       headers = c("TWFE", "Pooled OLS", "Bank Trends", "Double Cluster"),
       se.below = TRUE)

# =============================================================
# Final interpretation
# =============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== FINAL RESULTS ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
beta <- coef(mod1)["treat_x_post"]
pval <- pvalue(mod1)["treat_x_post"]
cat(sprintf("Main DID estimate: %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("p-value: %.4f\n", pval))
if (pval < 0.05) {
  if (beta > 0) {
    cat("CONCLUSION: TARP recipients experienced significantly HIGHER NPL ratios\n")
    cat("post-injection, consistent with increased risk-taking (moral hazard).\n")
  } else {
    cat("CONCLUSION: TARP recipients experienced significantly LOWER NPL ratios\n")
    cat("post-injection, consistent with reduced risk-taking (stabilization).\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("CONCLUSION: No statistically significant effect of TARP on NPL ratios.\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Positive DID coefficient.** The treatment effect (treat_x_post) should be positive, indicating that TARP recipient banks experienced a larger increase in non-performing loan ratios relative to non-recipients after capital injections.

**Expected magnitude:** Given the NPL ratios appear centered around 1.0 in the preview (likely in percentage points), I expect a DID coefficient in the range of **0.3–0.8 percentage points** — economically meaningful but not enormous, reflecting the moral hazard channel whereby capital cushions from TARP reduced banks' incentives to manage risk conservatively.

**Rationale:**
1. **Moral hazard theory:** Government capital injections create a safety net, encouraging risk-taking. Banks may lend more aggressively or delay writing off bad loans.
2. **Empirical literature:** Studies (e.g., Duchin & Sosyura 2014) find TARP recipients originated riskier loans post-injection. A positive coefficient aligns with this.
3. **Pre-trends:** I expect the event-study coefficients to be close to zero and statistically insignificant in the pre-treatment periods, validating the parallel trends assumption. Post-treatment coefficients should turn positive and potentially grow over time as risk-taking materializes in NPL ratios with a lag.
4. **Robustness:** The result should be robust across specifications (bank-specific trends, double-clustering), though magnitude may attenuate slightly with bank-specific trends if there were differential pre-existing trajectories.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=TARP recipients, control=non-recipients; parallel pre-trends required
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: TARP banks show higher NPL ratios post-injection, consistent with moral hazard
_ground_truth.main_effect: 20bp increase in NPL ratio for TARP banks
